blocks.h2: Smell Gas in Your Elgin Home? Start Here
blocks.intro: Your safety comes before the repair:

steps.h3: 1. Walk Out, Leave the Door Open Behind You
steps.body: Take people and pets outside. Skip the windows and don't go back for belongings.
Flipping a switch, ringing a doorbell or starting a car in an attached garage can create a spark.

steps.h3: 3. Phone Nicor Gas or 911 From the Sidewalk
steps.body: Make the call once you're well away from the house.
When the utility says it's safe to go back in, we locate the leak and repair it.

blocks.h2: Is Your Elgin Gas Piping Telling You Something?

tiles.h3: A Smell That Comes and Goes
tiles.body: A faint odor near the furnace, water heater or dryer that you notice now and then is worth a test. Small leaks at fittings often smell intermittent.

tiles.h3: Dead Grass Over a Buried Line
tiles.body: Gas leaking from an underground line to a grill or detached garage can kill the grass above it.
A stove that won't hold a strong blue flame or a water heater that keeps losing its pilot can point to a supply problem.
If Nicor Gas found a leak and red-tagged an appliance or the meter, the house piping has to be repaired and tested before service comes back.

bodies: When the utility finds a leak inside the house, it shuts off service and leaves the repair to you. We come in, test the piping section by section, and pinpoint the fitting, valve or connector that's leaking. Electronic detectors find it, and a soap test confirms it.

After the repair, the whole system is pressure-tested and the results are documented, so the utility can restore service. In Elgin's older homes, we also check for old branches that were never capped properly after an appliance was removed.

blocks.h2: What We Find in Elgin Gas Piping
blocks.intro: Some Elgin houses have gas piping that has been added to for more than a century.

items.body: Homes near downtown sometimes have pipe that once fed gas lights, old stoves or space heaters. If those branches weren't capped and tested, they're a risk.
Black iron pipe itself lasts a long time. The weak points are threaded unions and old plug valves, which loosen or stiffen with age.
A grill line or dryer branch added years ago without a permit is one of the most common leak sources we find.
Old uncoated brass connectors can crack where they bend. We swap them for coated stainless ones.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: Gas work done right, then tested.

steps.body: Gas line work should be done by a licensed pro. Ours are licensed and trained for it.
We find the problem, then give you a flat price.
Before the gas goes back on.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: Nicor Gas shut off my gas. What happens now?
items.preview: The house piping has to be repaired and pressure-tested before service is restored.
items.answer: The utility found a leak on your side of the meter. We find and repair it, pressure-test the system and give you what the utility needs to turn service back on.

items.q: Is a faint gas smell an emergency?
items.preview: Treat any gas smell seriously. Leave and call first.
items.answer: Yes. Even a faint smell can mean gas is collecting somewhere. Leave, call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside and let them decide. Then call us for the repair.

items.q: Can a gas leak be underground?
items.preview: Yes, on buried lines to grills, garages or outbuildings.
items.answer: Yes. Lines running to a grill, a detached garage or a pool heater are often buried. We can test and locate leaks on those lines too.

items.q: Do I need a permit for a gas repair in Elgin?
items.preview: Some repairs do. We'll tell you what applies.
items.answer: It depends on the work. Replacing a section of pipe or adding a line usually needs a permit. We'll explain what applies to your job.

items.q: How much does gas line repair cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on the leak's location and the fix. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the leak is, how much pipe needs work and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
